To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the best method for multi-label classification is the optimal thresholding, which is followed by score-driven thresholding.

1) threshold selection methods that consider the operating conditions are the best performing; 2) threshold selection methods are not sensitive to the number of labels; 3) the best performing thresholding methods are score-driven and one-optimal; 4) thresholding methods are more robust when using a larger training set and a smaller test set; 5) thresholding methods perform better when using an equal number of relevant and irrelevant labels.

(1) the optimal thresholding method outperforms all other thresholding methods in most of the datasets, (2) the score-driven thresholding method outperform the one optimal thresholding method in most of the dataset and (3) the one optimal threshold method is the most robust thresholding method.
